messages.author: 2330bbb33122f310
messages.subject: Plots from user defined SPDE function
parts:
Based on help from Finn in a previous thread on user defined functions, I am now trying an SPDE function.

The idea is to state main results and plots from a particular SPDE model (Kronecker product space-time) with various data. The JSS-paper (3.2) gives a good starting point, and I simply reorder my data into a list mydata (mydata$y, mydata$station.loc, mydata$station.id, mydata$time) which is the basic argument of the SPDE function.

The function is then defined using pieces of jss-code. Now, INLA does give results. The current problem is plotting and images. For the moment the program stops with the message "Error in plot.new() : figure margins too large". A previous version did return plots, but not images. I have not sufficient knowledge of R and INLA to see where the problems arise. Can anyone help me?

Code and a small data set is enclosed.

In relation to this I have questions about scales. Is there any suitable scale for coordinates and time? In my program I scaled coordinates to (0,1)^2 and time to (0,100) as seen from other code. I guess it would be better with unscaled measures? Otherwise, the mesh parameters should be adjusted according to scale? 

At a later stage I need plotting of borders from shapefiles onto INLA-plots.  How can that be done?

Kind regards
Øyvind

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Plots from user defined SPDE function
parts:
To better control the mesh resolution in real world terms it's easiest to use a common coordinate system. Which one to use depends on the size of the domain to some extent (large domains are best done on a sphere and not in a flat projection) but in your case I would guess that converting to km should be reasonable. You could then use the same max.edge value for each mesh, as that would then also be measured in km.

The latest versions of the package has some built-in support for this, if you already have the CRS information from a shapefile or similar. Inla.mesh.2d, inla.spde.make.A etc can take SpatialPoints and SpatialPolygons objects as input, and if inla.mesh.2d is given a CRS, the mesh will be built in that coordinate system, with the inputs automatically transformed to that system.  This is quite a new and not yet very much advertised or tested feature, so if you do use it, please let me know if it does or does not work for you!

For some CRS strings, using km is as easy as including units=km in the string. The helper function call
  crs=inla.CRS(myproj4string, args =list(units="km"))
works for many CRS specifications, but do double-check that the resulting CRS object means what you want it to mean.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Plots from user defined SPDE function
parts:
Thanks Finn. 

I understand that per se there is no need of adjusting mesh parameters (absolute distances and angles) for different regions of the same field as long as the same coordinate system is applied. In my case that is UTM32. I will test the CRS-functionality at a later stage.

What might need adjustment is the number of plotting points on which the level plots are based. The number of points per square km should be kept constant to retain spatial resolution. However, such adjustment does not change my plots substantially.

The basic conclusion from my plotting exercise is that my choice of model is lousy.  The estimation summaries say that the model for the small region --- showing detail that I would like to see --- is based on insignificant spde parameters, while the models for the larger regions without detail are all highly significant. 

My task now is to find other spatio-temporal models that INLA can deal with, and select among them according to out-of-sample predictive ability. A model function, with which both models and data support can be adjusted easily, facilitates the analysis of a considerable number of alternatives. 

I will return with some code in a few days. 

Perhaps needless to say: I do not expect the INLA team to provide such functions. It is the researchers' task to sweep across the available alternatives and choose among the better ones. 

Best
Øyvind

messages.author: 2330bbb33122f310
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Plots from user defined SPDE function
parts:
I do not understand what you mean, Finn.

Some explanation of my setting seems required.

My data comprise 3 points in time and 5758 points in space. The goal is to provide predictions for a 4th point in time at all points in space. A model with good off-sample predictions is then needed. To find it, I will test candidates on a subset of observations that has not been applied in estimation. Thus, I have two types of predictions. My only lattice is the one used in the construction of the level plots. 

The model I have run is a Kronecker product space-time model with 3 replicated spatial fields. A base alternative is of course a model with spatial dummies replacing the spatial field. An obvious alternative would be a three-dimensional SPDE-field, but that does not exist yet? My next alternative is two different likelihoods with

y_1 ~ f(s_1) + ...,    y_{t} - y_{t-1}  ~ g(s_t) + ...  for t=(2,3)

where s_2 and s_3 are replicate fields with the same hyper parameters, and s_1 has parameters of its own. 


Any other idea? 

Kind regards
Øyvind
